abstract: Lysine acetyltransferase (KAT) enzymes including the p300, MYST, and GCN5 families play major roles in modulating the structure of chromatin and regulating transcription. Because of their dysregulation in various disease states including cancer, efforts to develop inhibitors of KATs have steadily gained momentum. Here we provide an overview of recent progress on the development of high quality chemical probes of the p300 and MYST family of KATs and how they are emerging as useful tools for basic and translational investigation.
